newsitem.title: EU: EC REPORT WEEKLY DIARY FOR MONDAY, OCT 21 - SUNDAY, OCT 27.
newsitem.headline: EC REPORT WEEKLY DIARY FOR MONDAY, OCT 21 - SUNDAY, OCT 27.

text.p: HIGHLIGHTS

STRASBOURG - EP holds plenary session (Monday-Friday); Irish Foreign Minister report on the outcome of the Dublin summit and European Commission President Santer presents Commission's annual programme for 1997 (Tuesday).
STRASBOURG - European Commission holds regular weekly meeting (Wednesday); discussions include Montii's report on taxation.
DUBLIN - EU housing ministers hold informal meeting (Thursday-Friday); discussions on the positive impact housing policy can have in helping to counteract and prevent social exclusion.
LUXEMBOURG - EU internal market ministers meet (Friday); presentation of white paper on approximation of the laws of central and eastern European countries in the field of the internal market.
SOFIA - Bulgaria holds its second post-communist presidential election (Sunday).
MONDAY, OCTOBER 21

MOSCOW (NEW ITEM) - European Commissioner Cresson on official visit; meets Russian Deputy Prime Minister Vladimir Fortov and Russian Spatial agency Chairman Yu Koptev; addresses Lomonossov Universoty and the Douma.
STRASBOURG (EXPANDED ITEM) - EP holds plenary session (first of five days).
Agenda includes:
- (1700/1500 GMT) Armelle Guiebertiere report on a European guarantee fund to promote cinema and television production.
- Nana Mouskouri recommendation on the establishment of a support programme in the field of books and reading ("Ariane").
- Fransisco Javier Sanz Fernandez report on Europe's cultural heritage: programme to encourage its preservation and the estension of its influence.
- Nicole Fontaine recommendation on the free movement of doctors and recognition of their diplomas, certificates and other qualifications.
- (NEW ITEM) Julio Anoveros trias De Bes report on the Commission's green paper on legal protection in the single market.
STRASBOURG (NEW ITEM) - Following EP committees meet:
(1800/1600 GMT) Institutional Affairs;
(1900/1700 GMT) Agriculture;
Budget;
Transport;
Youth.

BRUSSELS - European Handicaped Action (AEH), Confederation of European Firms Initiatives and Cooperatives for Psychially Disabled (CEFEC), European Union Group of the International Organisation for the Provision of Work for Handicaped Persons (EUG-IPWH) hold joint conference on "Labour Market 2000" (1030/0830 GMT). Venue: Palais des Congres. Contact: AEH (49) 228 820 930.

STRASBOURG - Confederation of European Paper Industries (CEPI) holds conference on "Forest management and paper growing cooperation" (0830/0630 GMT) (and Tuesday). European Commissioner Fischler gives address on "The forestry activities of the EU as a contribution to the sustainable management and multi-functional role of the European forests. Venue: Hilton Hotel. Contact: CEPI (322) 627 4911.

THE HAGUE (NEW ITEM) - NATO Secretary General Javier Solana on official visit; meets Dutch Queen Beatrix, Prime Minister Wim Kok, Foreign Minister Hans Van Mierlo and Defence Minister Joris Voorhoeve.
TUESDAY, OCTOBER 22
STRASBOURG (EXPANDED ITEM) - EP holds plenary session (second of five days).
Agenda includes:
- (0915/0715 GMT) Irish Foreign Minister report on the outcome of the Dublin summit.
- European Commission President Santer presents Commission's annual work programme for 1997.
- Open debate on:
- Motion for a resolution on the implementation of the Community budget for 1996;
- Laurens Jan Brinkhorst report on the 1997 budget - section III;
- Juan Manuel Fabra Valles report on the 1997 budget - other sections;
- Giansily report on the ECSC budget for 1997.
- (1200/1000 GMT) Votes on:
- Reports under the cooperation, codecision and assent procedures;
- Motions for resolutions on which the debate is closed;
- (NEW ITEM) Werner Lange report on public contracts.
- (NEW ITEM) (1500/1300 GMT) European Commissioner Oreja holds news conference on the European cinema forum.
- (1730/1530 GMT) Question time by the Commission.
- Ria Oomen-Ruijten recommendation on misleading advertising so as to include comparative advertising.
- Danilo Poggiolini recommendation on the adoption of a programme of Community action on health monitoring in the framework for action in the field of public health.
- Karl Heinz Florenz report on the European Community Water Policy.
- Bermond d'Ars report on the application of the rules on competition to the postal sector.
STRASBOURG (NEW ITEM) - Following EP committees meet:
(1600/1400 GMT) Environment;
Rules of Procedure;
(1730/1530 GMT) Economic;
External Economic Relations;
Fisheries.

BRUSSELS - Union of Industrial and Employers' Confederation of Europe (UNICE) hold news conference on "What transport policy for Europe?" (1100/0900 GMT). Venue: UNICE, rue Joseph II. Contact: UNICE (322) 237 6511.
BRUSSELS - The European Aviation Club lunchtime meeting with British Airways Chief Executive Bob Ayling (1230/1030 GMT). Venue: Amigo Hotel. Contact: The European Aviation Club (322) 633 6030.
WEDNESDAY, OCTOBER 23
STRASBOURG (NEW ITEM) - European Commission holds regular weekly meeting (1500/1300 GMT).
Provisional agenda includes:
- State aids.
- European Commissioner Monti report on taxation.
- European Commissioner Brittan communication on conclusions of information technology.
- European Commissioner Bjerregaard communication on the implementation of the Community's environment legislation.
- European Commissioner Wulf-Mathies communication on structural funds for the second period programme under Objective 2 for 1997-1999.
STRASBOURG (EXPANDED ITEM) - EP holds plenary session (third of five days).
Agenda includes:
- (0900/0700 GMT) Council declaration following its meeting in Dublin on 5 October 1996.
- Council Declaration concerning events to mark the International Day for the Elimination of Poverty.
- (1200/1000 GMT) Votes on:
- Reports under the cooperation, codecision and assent procedures;
- Klaus Heiner Lehne, Glyn Ford and Milan Linzer reports;
- Motions for resolutions on which the debate is closed.
- (NEW ITEM) Rinaldo Bontempi report on the protection of the EU's financial interests.
- Joint debate on the European Association EU/Slovenia Agreement.
- Question time on a plan of action for Russia.
- Diemut Theato report on the setting up of an employment anf labour market policy.
- Diemut Theato report on on-the-spot checks and inspections by the Commission for the detection of frauds and irregularities detrimental to the financial interests of the European Communities.
- Nikitas Kaklamanis report on marine equipment.
- Spalato Bellere report on road worthiness test for motor vehicles and their trailers.
- Question time on the fourth framework programme for R&TD activities.

STRASBOURG (NEW ITEM) - His Holiness the Dali Lama meets EP President Klaus Haensch, Commission President Santer, European Commissioner Bonino, MEPs Pauline Green, Wilfried Martens, Gijs De Vreis, Claudia Roth and Catherine Lalumiere; attends joint meeting of Foreign Affairs, Economic and External Relations and Development Committees at 1630/1430 GMT.
STRASBOURG (NEW ITEM) - EP Committee into Fraud in Transit meets at 1500/1300 GMT.

STRASBOURG (NEW ITEM) - The Aerospace Intergroup holds conference on "The role of the equipment sector in the aerospace industry in Europe" (1700/1500 GMT). Venue: EP, Pal 3. Contact: Lucas Aardenburg (322) 775 8110.
THURSDAY, OCTOBER 24
DUBLIN (EXPANDED ITEM) - EU housing ministers hold informal meeting (0900/0800 GMT) (and Friday). European Commissioner Flynn attends.

Discussions include: the positive impact housing policy can have in helping to counteract and prevent social exclusion; the importance of housing as an element in the comprehensive approach necessary to address the problems of social exclusion. Closing news conference on Friday at 1345/1245 GMT. Venue: Dublin Castle.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Commission President Santer and Commissioner van den Broek meet Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok.
STRASBOURG (NEW ITEM) - EP holds plenary session (fourth of five days).
Agenda includes:
- Connected with the budget;
- On reports under the cooperation, codecision and assent procedures;
- On motions for resolutions on which the debate is closed.
- (1500/1300 GMT) Items in the news.
- (1800/1600 GMT) Joint debate:
- Fransisca Bennasar Tous report on a first multiannual programme to assist European tourism (PHILOXENIA);
- Eolo Parodi report on Community measures affecting tourism;
- Lyndon Harrison report on the evaluation of Community action plan to assist tourism 1993-1995.
- Erich Farthoher report on railway's.
STRASBOURG (NEW ITEM) - His Holiness the Dalai Lama holds news conference at 1030/0830 GMT. Venue: IPE3 press room.

BRUSSELS - European Metaworkers' Federation (EMF) holds second collective bargaining conference (and Friday). Agenda includes: trade unions in a globalised economy; social movements in a changing Europe; European economic policy, aimed at lasting growth, social equality and competitiveness. Venue: ETUC, 155 Blvd Emile Jacqmain. Contact: EMF (322) 217 2747.

BRUSSELS - Centre for European Policy Studies (CEPS) holds lunchtime seminar on "Switzerland-EU: the current state of play" (1315/1115 GMT). Speaker is: Swiss Ambassador to the EU Alexis Lautenberg. Venue: place du Congres. Contact: Anne-Marie Boudou (322) 229 3911.
MADRID - European Investment Bank (EIB) holds forum on "The Mediterranean: a space for partnership" at 1500/1300 GMT (and Friday).
Agenda includes:
- The Mediterranean, a common destiny:
- The EU's Mediterranean policy: from cooperation to partnership;
- The sea, water and cities: preserving a common heritage.
- An area for joint development:
- The dynamic role of trans-national projects;
- The banking sector and north-south partnership.

Speakers include: EIB President Sir Brian Unwin; European Commissioner for Relations with the Mediterranean Manuel Marin; MEP Willy De Clercq; Egyptian Minister of State for Economic Affairs Youssef Boutros-Ghali; Greek Deputy Foreign Minister George Romeos; Jordanian Planning Minister Rima Khalaf; Barcelona Mayor and EU Committee of the Regions President Pasqual Maragall. Contact: Yvonne Berghorst, EIB (352) 4379 3154.
FRIDAY, OCTOBER 25
LUXEMBOURG (EXPANDED ITEM) - Internal Market Council.
Provisional agenda includes:
- White paper on approximation of the laws of central and eastern European countries in the field of the internal market - preparation for the meeting with central and eastern European countries.
- Adoption of draft Council resolution on the simplification and rationalisation of the Community's regulations and customs procedures.
- The "Robert Schuman" action.
- Commission communication to the Council, EP and Economic and Social Committee on the transparency mechanism for national regulations concerning the information society.
STRASBOURG (EXPANDED ITEM) - EP holds plenary session (last of five days).
Agenda includes:
- (0900/0700 GMT) Patricia McKenna report on Commission report on monitoring the common fisheries policy.
- Votes on:
- Any procedures without report;
- Any reports without debate;
- Motions for resolutions on which the debate is closed.
- Hindley report on the interim agreement on trade between the EU and Belarus.
- Joint debate:
- (NEW ITEM) Peter Kittelman report on U.S. Helms/Bruton law affecting trade with Cuba.
- Heinz Kindermann report on Community structural assistance in the fisheries and aquaculture sector;
- Carmen Fraga Estevez on Mediterranean issues;
- Gerard d'Aboville on fisheries agreement between the EC and Seychelles;
- Pat the Cope Gallagher on the Commission communication on the implementation of technical measures in the common fisheries policy;
- Liam Hyland report on the creation of European Rural Charter;
- Alan Leslie Gillis report on trade agreements for certain goods resulting from the processing of agricultural products.

BRUSSELS - European Mortgage Federation holds annual general assembly on "From the internal market to the single currency" at 0900/0700 GMT. News conference at 1200/1000 GMT. Agenda includes; the European central bank and its operations; the consumer and the single currency; the capital market and the European Monetary Union. Speakers include: European Monetary Institute Director General Robert Raymond; European Commissioner Bonino and Deutsche Bundesbank Board Member Otmar Issing. Venue: General de Banque, 1 rue de la Chancellerie. Contact: European Mortgage Federation (322) 285 4030.
SATURDAY, OCTOBER 26
No events scheduled.
SUNDAY, OCTOBER 27
- European summer time ends - Central European time changes from GMT +2 to GMT +1.
SOFIA - Bulgaria holds its second post-communist presidential election.
